title: Simplifying Expressions
seo_title: Grade 7 Simplifying Expressions Worksheets: Like Terms, Distributive Property and Factoring
standard_text: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 simplifying expressions worksheets: combine like terms, use the distributive property, subtract groups, factor with the GCF, work with fraction and decimal coefficients, and write equivalent expressions for real situations. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: Combine only like terms, and multiply every term inside the parentheses.
body_html:
Like terms

Like terms have the same variable part. 4x and 2x are like terms. 4x and 3 are not. To simplify, add the coefficients of like terms and keep the variable.

The distributive property

a(b + c) = ab + ac. Multiply the number outside by every term inside. A minus sign in front of a group changes the sign of every term: −(2x + 1) = −2x − 1.

SkillExpressionSimplified
Combine like terms4x + 3 + 2x6x + 3
Distribute3(2x − 5)6x − 15

Factor12x + 84(3x + 2)
Example

Simplify 3(2x − 1) + 4x + 7.

Distribute: 6x − 3 + 4x + 7.

Combine: 6x + 4x = 10x and −3 + 7 = 4.

Answer: 10x + 4

Example

A price p goes up 5%. Write the new price two ways.

Price plus 5% of the price: p + 0.05p.

Combine: 1.05p.

Answer: p + 0.05p = 1.05p

Common mistakes

  • Adding unlike terms: 4x + 3 is not 7x.
  • Distributing to one term: 3(2x − 5) is 6x − 15, not 6x − 5.
  • Subtracting a group: (5x + 3) − (2x + 1) is 3x + 2, not 3x + 4.

faq.a: Terms with the same variable part. 5x and −2x are like terms, so 5x − 2x = 3x. 5x and 5 are not like terms.

faq.q: How do you use the distributive property?
faq.a: Multiply the number outside the parentheses by every term inside: 4(2x − 3) = 8x − 12.

faq.q: How do you subtract an expression in parentheses?
faq.a: Change the sign of every term in the group: (7x + 2) − (3x + 4) = 7x + 2 − 3x − 4 = 4x − 2.

faq.q: How do you factor a linear expression?
faq.a: Find the greatest common factor of the terms and divide each term by it: 15x − 10 = 5(3x − 2). Check by distributing.

items.q: What is the coefficient of x in 7 − 5x?
items.e: The coefficient is the number multiplying x, including its sign: 7 − 5x = 7 + (−5)x.
Terms are separated by + and − signs: 3x, −4 and 2y.

items.q: What is the constant term in 6a − 11?
items.e: The constant term is the number with no variable. Keep its sign: −11.
5x + 3x = 8x and the 2 stays: 8x + 2.
x + 3x = 4x and 4y − y = 3y. x-terms and y-terms are not like terms, so the answer is 4x + 3y.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand 3(x + 4).
items.e: Multiply 3 by each term: 3 × x = 3x and 3 × 4 = 12. So 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12. Not 3x + 4: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand 5(2x − 3).
items.e: Multiply 5 by each term: 5 × 2x = 10x and 5 × (−3) = −15. So 5(2x − 3) = 10x − 15. Not 10x − 3: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand 4(3x + 7).
items.e: Multiply 4 by each term: 4 × 3x = 12x and 4 × 7 = 28. So 4(3x + 7) = 12x + 28. Not 12x + 7: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand 2(6x − 1).
items.e: Multiply 2 by each term: 2 × 6x = 12x and 2 × (−1) = −2. So 2(6x − 1) = 12x − 2. Not 12x − 1: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand −2(x + 5).
items.e: Multiply −2 by each term: −2 × x = −2x and −2 × 5 = −10. So −2(x + 5) = −2x − 10. Not −2x + 5: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand −3(2x − 4).
items.e: Multiply −3 by each term: −3 × 2x = −6x and −3 × (−4) = 12. So −3(2x − 4) = −6x + 12. Not −6x − 4: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand 6(x − 8).
items.e: Multiply 6 by each term: 6 × x = 6x and 6 × (−8) = −48. So 6(x − 8) = 6x − 48. Not 6x − 8: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand −4(5x + 1).
items.e: Multiply −4 by each term: −4 × 5x = −20x and −4 × 1 = −4. So −4(5x + 1) = −20x − 4. Not −20x + 1: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand 7(2x + 3).
items.e: Multiply 7 by each term: 7 × 2x = 14x and 7 × 3 = 21. So 7(2x + 3) = 14x + 21. Not 14x + 3: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand −(3x − 6).
items.e: Multiply −1 by each term: −1 × 3x = −3x and −1 × (−6) = 6. So −(3x − 6) = −3x + 6. Not −3x − 6: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand 10(0.5x + 2).
items.e: Multiply 10 by each term: 10 × 0.5x = 5x and 10 × 2 = 20. So 10(0.5x + 2) = 5x + 20. Not 5x + 2: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand 0.5(4x − 6).
items.e: Multiply 0.5 by each term: 0.5 × 4x = 2x and 0.5 × (−6) = −3. So 0.5(4x − 6) = 2x − 3. Not 2x − 6: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand −5(3x + 2).
items.e: Multiply −5 by each term: −5 × 3x = −15x and −5 × 2 = −10. So −5(3x + 2) = −15x − 10. Not −15x + 2: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand 8(−x + 4).
items.e: Multiply 8 by each term: 8 × (−x) = −8x and 8 × 4 = 32. So 8(−x + 4) = −8x + 32. Not −8x + 4: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand 1.5(2x + 6).
items.e: Multiply 1.5 by each term: 1.5 × 2x = 3x and 1.5 × 6 = 9. So 1.5(2x + 6) = 3x + 9. Not 3x + 6: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand −6(−2x + 3).
items.e: Multiply −6 by each term: −6 × (−2x) = 12x and −6 × 3 = −18. So −6(−2x + 3) = 12x − 18. Not 12x + 3: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand 12(6x + 8).
items.e: Multiply 12 by each term: 12 × 6x = 3x and 12 × 8 = 4. So 12(6x + 8) = 3x + 4. Not 3x + 8: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand 23(9x − 3).
items.e: Multiply 23 by each term: 23 × 9x = 6x and 23 × (−3) = −2. So 23(9x − 3) = 6x − 2. Not 6x − 3: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand −14(8x + 12).
items.e: Multiply −14 by each term: −14 × 8x = −2x and −14 × 12 = −3. So −14(8x + 12) = −2x − 3. Not −2x + 12: multiply both terms, not just the first.

items.q: Use the distributive property to expand 35(10x + 5).
items.e: Multiply 35 by each term: 35 × 10x = 6x and 35 × 5 = 3. So 35(10x + 5) = 6x + 3. Not 6x + 5: multiply both terms, not just the first.

Distribute first: 3(2x − 1) = 6x − 3. Then combine like terms: x + 3.

Distribute first: −3(2x − 5) = −6x + 15. Then combine like terms: −5x + 19.
Subtracting a group subtracts every term: (5x + 3) − (2x + 1) = 5x + 3 − 2x − 1. Combine: 3x + 2. Not 3x + 4: the minus sign must reach both terms.
Subtracting a group subtracts every term: (7x − 2) − (3x + 4) = 7x − 2 − 3x − 4. Combine: 4x − 6. Not 4x + 2: the minus sign must reach both terms.
Subtracting a group subtracts every term: (4x + 6) − (x − 5) = 4x + 6 − x + 5. Combine: 3x + 11. Not 3x + 1: the minus sign must reach both terms.
Subtracting a group subtracts every term: (9x + 1) − (9x + 8) = 9x + 1 − 9x − 8. Combine: −7. Not 9: the minus sign must reach both terms.
Subtracting a group subtracts every term: (3x − 4) − (−2x − 6) = 3x − 4 + 2x + 6. Combine: 5x + 2. Not 5x − 10: the minus sign must reach both terms.
Subtracting a group subtracts every term: (6x) − (2x + 7) = 6x − 2x − 7. Combine: 4x − 7. Not 4x + 7: the minus sign must reach both terms.

The GCF of 6 and 15 is 3. 6x ÷ 3 = 2x and 15 ÷ 3 = 5, so 6x + 15 = 3(2x + 5). Check by distributing.
The GCF of 12 and 8 is 4. 12x ÷ 4 = 3x and −8 ÷ 4 = −2, so 12x − 8 = 4(3x − 2). Check by distributing.
The GCF of 5 and 20 is 5. 5x ÷ 5 = x and 20 ÷ 5 = 4, so 5x + 20 = 5(x + 4). Check by distributing.
The GCF of 12 and 18 is 6. 12x ÷ 6 = 2x and −18 ÷ 6 = −3, so 12x − 18 = 6(2x − 3). Check by distributing.
The GCF of 21 and 7 is 7. 21x ÷ 7 = 3x and 7 ÷ 7 = 1, so 21x + 7 = 7(3x + 1). Check by distributing.
The GCF of 10 and 18 is 2. 10x ÷ 2 = 5x and 18 ÷ 2 = 9, so 10x + 18 = 2(5x + 9). Check by distributing.
The GCF of 8 and 24 is 8. 8x ÷ 8 = x and −24 ÷ 8 = −3, so 8x − 24 = 8(x − 3). Check by distributing.
The GCF of 18 and 9 is 9. 18x ÷ 9 = 2x and 9 ÷ 9 = 1, so 18x + 9 = 9(2x + 1). Check by distributing.
The GCF of 20 and 12 is 4. 20x ÷ 4 = 5x and 12 ÷ 4 = 3, so 20x + 12 = 4(5x + 3). Check by distributing.
The GCF of 30 and 70 is 10. 30x ÷ 10 = 3x and −70 ÷ 10 = −7, so 30x − 70 = 10(3x − 7). Check by distributing.

items.e: Use a common denominator: 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4, so the answer is 3/4 x.

items.q: Simplify 2(x + 12) + 12x.
c: 52x + 12
items.e: 2(x + 1/2) = 2x + 1. Then 2x + 1/2 x = 5/2 x. The answer is 5/2 x + 1.

items.q: A price p goes up by 5%. Which expression shows the new price?
items.e: p + 0.05p = 1.05p. Both show the price plus 5% of the price.

items.q: A jacket costs j dollars and is 20% off. Which expression shows the sale price?
items.e: j − 0.2j = 0.8j. You pay 80% of the price.

items.e: 4(t + 3) = 4t + 12. Each friend pays t + 3.

items.q: Jon says 2(x + 5) = 2x + 5. What mistake did he make?
c: He should have added 2 and 5 first.
items.e: The 2 multiplies both terms: 2(x + 5) = 2x + 10.

items.q: A garden is w meters wide. Its length is 3 meters less than twice the width. Which expression is the perimeter?
A gym membership costs $25 a month plus a $10 fee each month for classes. Which expression shows the cost for m months?
items.e: Each month costs 25 + 10 = 35 dollars, so m months cost 35m. 25m + 10m = 35m too.
